long_biography.plain_text:
In 2000, Moran helped create the charitable institution bearing her husband's name and became its founding president. The couple supplied some of the opening capital; JM Family Enterprises made a separate contribution and promised future support tied to company profits. She remained in charge after Jim died in 2007, overseeing programmes for education, families and community services across Florida. IRS filings show that this full-time governance position is unpaid.

One of her largest later initiatives came when she and the foundation together committed $100 million to Florida State University. The gift illustrates her role but not the composition of her fortune. Jim built JM Family through vehicle distribution and related businesses, then left the enterprise to his descendants; a trust associated with his three children continues to own it. Nothing reliable reviewed identifies an equity interest, estate allocation or investment portfolio held by Jan. Her own donations demonstrate substantial means, while the company's revenue and operating property, plus the charity's securities and endowment, remain outside any calculation of her personal wealth.
